Question Choices: A square has a side length of 9 meters. What is the perimeter of the square? (in meters)
Hints: A square has four equal sides, so multiply one side by 4.
Solution: All four sides equal 9. Perimeter=4 x 9=36 metres.

Question Choices: A rectangle has an area of 12 square centimeters and a perimeter of 14 centimeters. The rectangle is longer than it is wide. What are the length and width? (cm) Length: ___ cm. Width: ___ cm.
Hints: Find positive side lengths whose product is the area and whose sum is half the perimeter.
Solution: Half the perimeter is 14/2=7, so length+width=7. Their product must be 12. The factor pair 4 and 3 has both properties. Length is the larger:4;width 3. Check:area=4 x 3=12;perimeter=2 x(4+3)=14.

Question Choices: A rectangle has an area of 36 square meters and a perimeter of 26 meters. The rectangle is longer than it is wide. What are the length and width of the rectangle? (in m) Length: ___ m. Width: ___ m.
Hints: Find positive side lengths whose product is the area and whose sum is half the perimeter.
Solution: Half the perimeter is 26/2=13, so length+width=13. Their product must be 36. The factor pair 9 and 4 has both properties. Length is the larger:9;width 4. Check:area=9 x 4=36;perimeter=2 x(9+4)=26.

Question Choices: Select. A vegetable garden is 15 meters long and 6 meters wide. A flower garden is 12 meters long and 9 meters wide. Which garden has a larger area?: ~~vegetable-garden | flower-garden~~
Hints: Calculate both areas separately. Equal perimeter does not force equal area.
Solution: First area=15 x 6=90 square metres. Second area=12 x 9=108 square metres. 108>90, so the flower garden is larger.

Question Choices: Select. A gardener wants to build a rectangular fence around his flower bed. He has 30 meters of fencing. He notices two possible rectangles that both use all the fencing. Rectangle A - 6 m by 9 m. Rectangle B - 5 m by 10 m. He states that both use 30 meters of fencing, so they must have the same area. Is his statement correct?: ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Calculate both areas separately. Equal perimeter does not force equal area.
Solution: First area=6 x 9=54 square metres. Second area=5 x 10=50 square metres. Both perimeters are 30 metres, but 54!=50; equal perimeter does not mean equal area.
